evidence:
The implementation observations below supersede the pre-implementation context.
Both required slices completed on observed AArch64 seL4 QEMU evidence:

- External TCP client `01a08ff0-0bae-741e-9318-331fdafe0b96`: exact 4096-byte
  echo over application IO0 payloads and virtio-net, independently reconstructed
  at the frame peer, with handshake, FIN/ACK close, declared-port refusal,
  forbidden-egress denial, ARP/ICMP and normal resource teardown.
- Listener/lifetime `01a0ddaa-825f-7309-8508-ed49ffe33a8d`: all six mandatory
  automated acceptances passed under one `io_network_qualification_check`
  execution identity. `devloop eligible` returned true; `devloop complete`
  then reported `eligible: true, closed: true`. Its canonical record contains
  the exact requirements, helper, code, policy, inputs, target, image label,
  run epoch and observations, rather than a manual completion assertion.

The final qualification code digest was
`942af041a6904336d177031c3134be3d4d35ebef51fe8cfd3cf8a37a2fe993fb`,
with policy digest
`360b9cb40092114a2773d7d7cf6cb6e590ac9920da5e7850fe061afb1effd196`
and input digest
`8eb96db0a91dc3a0c2d096624cadb7a63601ace38908575d28ca53cb66b5fefe`.
The input selected `io_network_qualification_check`; target was
`aarch64-sel4-qemu-virt` and the suite image label was
`network-io0-tcp-qualification`.

Observed local and lifetime results:

- Separately declared `publisher-session` and `subscriber-session` performed
  real listen/connect/accept at `127.0.0.1:7447`, independently comparing
  4096/2048 bytes including split/coalesced opaque length-prefixed batches.
  No NIC was present. Seven authority refusals, a typed receive timeout followed
  by resumed traffic, notification waiting, EOF and normal cleanup were observed.
- A real client VM fault caused holder-bound socket and buffer reclamation,
  one actual loopback reset and a reset completion at the surviving client.
  Supervised restart advanced the service incarnation and exchanged fresh bytes.
- A closure-selected service fault occurred with payload work pending. Root
  reclaimed its holder resources; clients faulted on revoked mappings. Restarted
  clients and service exchanged fresh bytes and refused predecessor handles.
- An actual virtio-net reset settled an in-flight application request with typed
  RESET. A queued but not-yet-admitted RX request was settled as well. Device
  epochs advanced 1 to 2 and, after supervised restart, 2 to 3. The fresh external
  session exchanged and acknowledged all 4096 bytes and closed with FIN/ACK.
- Production-source host tests covered exact peer/holder/direction authority,
  bounded socket/queue/byte/timer/retry admission, backpressure, timeout, EOF,
  reset quarantine and stale completion rejection followed by fresh completion.
  The network host harness passed 14 tests and root host tests passed 346.

| External TCP | `687dabe7bed0e237ceb64530a08b5bde695148aac10eab78616fa3d95bd4f8da` |
| Local TCP | `ae7c37bd6bbfc7178cfc4cc169712b9785a4bccf7d3d6f24232f6e6f8bb0197c` |
| Client lifetime | `1a822ac8a8302070d94cdf07454d930c6a53ef23bbbdb3625b35065479438e4a` |
| Service fault in flight | `8eea6c1635820e8dc905ad138c1d852ca6f0a54a39fe63f5b8f2f3af518cc8fd` |
| Driver reset in flight | `4ca43c5afe00fb64bc26314b8b72dc9ac1b307674d3ebcb78293e08e54f9fee1` |

The aggregate also passed contracts, system-spec derivation, system-image builder,
legacy authority/link regressions, host/root tests, independent peer controls,
3077 marker/layout mutations, formatting, lint, maintained docs, Python lint and
spelling checks. No runtime claim relies on framebuffer output or logical packet
counts alone.

Limits: these are QEMU observations, not physical NIC/DMA containment or hardware
qualification. The controlled reset peer deliberately holds and abandons its
first 1024-byte session before accepting a new SYN; this is not transparent TCP
continuation or ordinary-server interoperability across reset. Native startup
rendezvous and silent live-client abandonment retain the documented limitations.
UDP/DNS, arbitrary external listeners, general smoltcp coverage, Zenoh parsing,
ROS/CDR and middleware interoperability remain separate work. No Git commit or
remote publication was performed as part of these observations.
